verdict: The full chain is proven end to end on real compute. Three documented limits were read, not assumed, and two of them would have broken the run.

limits_read_from_docs.rule_that_binds: 'If multiple services are used in one API call, the lower of the rate limits is applied.'
limits_read_from_docs.reason: the request sends diarize=true. Diarization is not optional - it is what separates 22 speakers, the difference between a transcript and unlabelled text.
limits_read_from_docs.headroom_reason: 9 slots under the cap absorb retries. Also, the VM has 2 vCPU - 25 concurrent workers would thrash below the vendor limit.
limits_read_from_docs.enterprise_tier: starts at 200 concurrent - not pursued, it costs money and Rule 2 forbids it

limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.limit: File size: Maximum 2 GB. 'For large video files, extract the audio stream first.'
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.status_if_unhandled: one unit is 3.00 GB ('10-03-2024 NHB+ Call - October Reading Offers Call - 1476x10') and would fail 100% of the time
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.mitigation: ffmpeg -vn -c:a copy -> lossless REMUX, no re-encode. Also cuts upload volume 183.92 GB -> 28.0 GB, a 85% reduction.
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.quality_impact: none - the AAC stream is copied bit for bit. Confirmed empirically: the MP3 and MP4 of the same call transcribe to 37027w/spk22 vs 36963w/spk21.
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.cost_impact: none - Deepgram bills per audio minute, not per byte
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.tension_with_g0: AGENTS.md §4 states 'No transcode is needed anywhere in this pipeline. If a proposal introduces one, it is solving a problem that does not exist.' The 3.00 GB file makes that true for exactly one unit. The general claim no longer holds.

limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.limit: Synchronous requests exceeding 10 minutes return 504 Gateway Timeout (Nova/Base/Enhanced).
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.measurement: longest call is 276 min (4.60 h); p95 is 229 min; median 177 min
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.margin: inside the limit, but the thinnest margin in the build. If observed processing time exceeds 8 min for any call, that is the signal to move to the async endpoint.

limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.limit: Deepgram does not store transcripts. The API response is the only opportunity to retrieve it.
limits_that_would_have_broken_the_run.consequence: receipts and transcripts MUST be written before the media is deleted. The runner enforces this order.

response_shape.note: my first parser invented metadata.duration.seconds and channels[0].paragraphs. Both were wrong. The RUN-PLAN had it right and I deviated, then tried to fix it by reading one sample instead of the spec.
response_shape.metadata_duration: a plain float in SECONDS - not an object
response_shape.metadata_model_info: object keyed by model UUID -> {name, version, arch}

measured_chain.transcript_opens: Alright, gang. Today is Monday, 04/18/2022. We have the world famous Mike Gandia with us.
measured_chain.throughput_note: 159 s for 1436 MB (9.0 MB/s) on the first file. This is Deepgram PROCESSING at ~40x realtime, NOT upload bandwidth - the VM network cap is 12500 Mbps (1562 MB/s) and we used 4.6% of it.

bugs_found_in_the_transport.cause: curl --data-binary @file loads the ENTIRE body into memory. 1436 MB exhausted it on a 7 GB box, and curl reports the misleading message 'option --data-binary'.
bugs_found_in_the_transport.fix: python urllib streaming from a file handle
bugs_found_in_the_transport.note: --data-binary @- did not fix it. Only real streaming does.

bugs_found_in_the_transport.symptom: Authorization header malformed, curl error pointed nowhere near the cause
bugs_found_in_the_transport.cause: Windows pipes send CRLF. read -r strips the \n but leaves the \r, so the key arrived as 41 characters instead of 40.
FALSE NEGATIVE. It is not a systemd unit on Ubuntu 24.04, so systemctl is-active returns inactive for a process that is running. ps shows it. Only a real fetch is the arbiter.

bugs_found_in_the_transport.symptom: apt-cache showed megacmd's libfuse2t64 dependency unavailable
bugs_found_in_the_transport.cause: apt-get update had not been run
bugs_found_in_the_transport.fix: apt-get update is mandatory before apt-cache

secrets: the Deepgram key arrives on STDIN, CR-stripped. Never argv, never a file, never logged. argv is visible in the process table and in this transcript.
